T-D550FC.verdict: STALE FOR THE RAY -- not reproduced, with a separating control
T-D550FC.how: REPL x3, the item's own fixture (PSET(75,60),9 : CIRCLE(60,60),15,6,-0.01,1.57)
T-D550FC.headline: ZEROBAS'S SPOKE ENDPOINT DIVERGES FROM THE REFERENCE AT NEAR-ZERO ANGLES
T-D550FC.reading: POINT(75,60)/POINT(75,59)/POINT(74,60) read '6 6 6' on vg8020, cf3300 AND zb
T-D550FC.why_not_a_heal: 🔴 (75,60) IS CENTRE + (15,0) -- a point ON THE ARC ITSELF, and the arc spans -0.01..1.57 which includes angle 0. So the CIRCLE paints that pixel whether or not the SPOKE reaches it. The row cannot separate the two writers, so agreement here is not evidence the endpoint agrees. Recorded unresolved rather than healed.
T-D550FC.instrument_note: ⚠️ AND MY FIRST DRAFT WAS NOT THE ITEM'S FIXTURE AT ALL -- it dropped the `PSET(75,60),9` seed, turning 'does colour 6 REACH and overwrite a pixel holding 9' into 'does the spoke paint the pixel'. Same coordinates, different experiment. Re-run verbatim before the confound above was even visible.
T-D550FC.what_would_settle_it: a point on the SPOKE but OFF the arc -- i.e. strictly inside radius 15 along the near-zero-angle ray -- or the banked full-plane capture the item was originally measured from (scratchpad/g4_arc_boundary_capture.json)
T-D550FC.reading_t17: y=60 at radii 5/9/13 (strictly inside the arc): '6 6 6' on vg8020, cf3300 AND zb. The SAME radii at y=59, where a (15,-1) ray would have to pass: '4 4 4' on all three. All three machines draw the spoke along y=60 and none rises.
T-D550FC.the_control_that_makes_it_mean_something: 🟢 A POSITIVE start angle (CIRCLE...,0.01,1.57) draws NO SPOKE, and the same y=60 points then read '4 4 4' on all three. THAT is what proves those pixels are the SPOKE's and not the arc's -- exactly the control tranche 16's row lacked, and without it this row would have been the same non-answer.
T-D550FC.residue: ⚠️ THE ENDPOINT PIXEL ITSELF REMAINS UNSEPARABLE -- centre+(15,0) lies on the arc, which paints it either way. So the filed claim is refuted for the RAY (13 of 15 pixels measured identical, and the y=59 alternative empty) and untested for the single last pixel. That is a much narrower claim than 'zerobas's spoke endpoint diverges', and the item should be restated to it rather than closed outright.

T-0DFFD6.verdict: NOT MEASURED -- my plane instrument counts data the screen may not show
T-0DFFD6.headline: THE ARC MASK DIVERGES AT LARGE RADII
T-0DFFD6.why: 🔴 `SCREEN 2:CLS` LEAVES 4923 SET PIXELS IN THE VG-8020's PATTERN TABLE AND 0 IN ZEROBAS'S. A whole-plane bit count therefore compares a reference baseline of 4923 against a zerobas baseline of 0, and an XOR against the empty plane is no better: where the figure sets a bit the leftover already set, nothing changes, so the count under-reports what was drawn (circle: ref XOR 275 vs zb 536 for the SAME figure).
T-0DFFD6.what_it_needs: the NAME table as well as the pattern table -- the leftover is probably unreferenced by the name table and therefore invisible, which is why the items' own figures are small (170/127/97/135). Counting the pattern table alone measures bytes the screen may never show.
T-0DFFD6.note: 🟢 zerobas's counts came out at exactly the filed REFERENCE values on all four rows (170, 127, 97, 135 against filed ref 170, 127, 97, 135) -- suggestive that all four healed, but NOT evidence, because the reference side of the same run is invalid.
